clue.text: Darts trophy put on sideboard at last

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the word sideboard

parts.note: the Ashes is the trophy contested by England and Australia at cricket

explanation.surface: A darts trophy is placed on top of a sideboard at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places ASHES after the D, read down or along. 'Darts' looks like the game but is the verb: it dashes about.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move quickly and suddenly, a synonym of rushing or hurrying along.

clue.text: A Tuscan city some mentioned for one seeking peace and quiet

indicators.note: some mentioned signals that the phrase is spoken, as some people say it

parts.note: A plus Pisa, the Tuscan city of the leaning tower

explanation.surface: A traveller heads for a Tuscan city in search of tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent 'a Pisa' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeaser is someone who placates others to keep the peace, avoiding conflict.

clue.text: Incline to avoid attention, having internal problems

indicators.note: having internal means the outer word holds the troubles inside it

parts.note: to hide is to keep out of sight
ills are troubles or problems

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a low profile, troubled by inner problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillside is a slope, the inclined side of a hill.

clue.text: Grass acted as informant, giving away name familiar to very few people

indicators.note: giving away means losing the letter that stands for name

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to police, so sung
arcane means known only to a few, secret

explanation.surface: A grass informed, betraying a name known to few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the informer of the surface but is the plant. 'giving away' cuts SUNG to SUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a tall tropical grass whose stems yield sugar.

clue.text: Group of creatures backing America to the limit

indicators.note: backing here means the short name for America is taken in reverse

parts.note: a border is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Someone supports America to the bitter end.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a suborder is a taxonomic rank, a grouping of related animals below an order.

clue.text: Briefly test out a modified tourist attraction

indicators.note: modified means the letters of the preceding words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A quick test of a revised tourist site is carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor is one of the most visited landmarks in the US.

clue.text: Bid made by opponent — not clubs, generally speaking

indicators.note: not means the letter for clubs is left out

parts.note: in bridge an overcall is a bid made after an opponent has opened
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: At bridge, an opponent bids but avoids clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: An overcall is a bridge term for a bid after the opposition has opened the bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall, as an adverb, means taking everything into account, broadly or generally.

clue.text: Cut short spoken examination relating to higher degree

indicators.note: spoken signals that the word is said aloud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is docked
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A spoken exam for a higher degree is abruptly ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' looks as if it describes the examination, but it applies to DOCKED, which sounds like DOCT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctoral describes things belonging to a doctorate, the highest university degree.

clue.text: Travelling at great speed? That's worrying

definitions.meaning: ... along means moving briskly and fast
..., from rattle, means disconcerting or unnerving

explanation.definitionFit: Rattling describes going at a brisk pace, and also means unsettling or alarming, from rattle someone.

clue.text: A player's heading ball towards goal, one awkward for the defence

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter, here that of player's

parts.note: a ball is round, so it gives the letter O

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A footballer heads the ball towards goal, causing trouble for the defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards' is a link. 'awkward' rearranges GOAL plus I into LOGIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written justification, a reasoned case made in support of one's views.

clue.text: Rhyming lines alternately in their accents

indicators.note: alternately takes every other letter of their accents, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Lines of verse are spoken with alternating accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercet is a group of three lines of verse, often rhyming together, as in terza rima.

clue.text: Husband's a useless cheat, abandoning daughter and wife

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
US is short for unserviceable, slang for useless

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out the letter that stands for daughter

parts.note: a fraud is a cheat or impostor

explanation.surface: A husband is a worthless cheat who walks out on his daughter and wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops D from FRAUD to leave FRAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausfrau is German for housewife, used in English for a homely married woman.

clue.text: Type of fuel ultimately leaving a stain

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word leaving

parts.note: to soil is to stain or dirty

explanation.surface: Some fuel spilt in the end leaves a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas oil is a kind of diesel fuel distilled from petroleum, used in heating and engines.

clue.text: Endless struggle to intercept phone line

indicators.note: to intercept is to come between, so the struggle sits inside the telephone word

parts.note: to dial is to phone someone

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter from the synonym for struggle

parts.note: agony is a violent struggle or anguish

explanation.surface: An endless battle is waged to tap a phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of the struggle word; 'to intercept' means coming between, so the shortened word sits inside the phone word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal is a slanting straight line joining opposite corners.

clue.text: Stuck in a valley, unable to move? Not half, after this?

definitions.text: Stuck in a valley, unable to move? Not half, after this?

parts.words: Stuck in a valley, unable to move? Not half, after this?
parts.note: a snowslide down a mountainside leaves people trapped in the valley below; not half is British slang for very much so

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in a valley wonders whether they are truly trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang meaning very much so, answering the question.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding down a mountain, which can bury and trap those below.

clue.text: Poor fellow eating fish

indicators.note: eating means the letters are swallowed inside the words Poor fellow

explanation.surface: A poor man is having fish for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like an anagram signal but is just part of the text holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often kept in ornamental ponds.

clue.text: Sequel of fine film?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
to shoot is to film

explanation.surface: A follow-up to a fine film is being considered.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a development that grows out of something, a consequence or spin-off.

clue.text: Chips in to provide shelter for a cow

parts.note: fries are chips, French fries

indicators.note: to provide shelter for means the outer word holds the letter A inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chips are served in a barn to give a cow shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the British word for French fries; 'to provide shelter for' wraps the clue's 'in' round A, giving IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a breed of black-and-white dairy cattle.

clue.text: Hit record with loud introduction

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
a log is a written record, as of a voyage

explanation.surface: A hit record opens with a loud intro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with loud introduction' means F comes before LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat or strike repeatedly with a whip or stick.

clue.text: Employer coming over in state of agitation gets very angry

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the agitation word

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic or agitation

indicators.note: coming over means the word is turned round

parts.note: a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: A boss turns up in a flap and loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns the employer word round, giving RESU; 'in' sets that inside the agitation word.
explanation.definitionFit: To flare up is to become suddenly enraged or to burst out angrily.

clue.text: Old Bill in rural parts claiming authority

indicators.note: in places the bill inside the reordered letters
parts suggests the letters are split up and rearranged

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: The police (the Old Bill) in the countryside assert their authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, but here it splits into two pieces. 'parts' gives ULAR plus R around the bill's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular means speaking like an oracle, with assumed authority and solemnity.

clue.text: Carpet in university accommodation, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a hall at Keele University in Staffordshire, England

explanation.surface: Carpet is being fitted in student halls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb, to reprimand. Keele is an English university, so a Keele hall is student housing.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them severely, and keelhauling is the old naval punishment used figuratively for a harsh scolding.

clue.text: Variety of glue OK to fix a protective cover

indicators.note: to fix means to set the letter A firmly within
variety of means a different arrangement of the following letters

explanation.surface: A different glue, OK for fixing a protective cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges GLUE OK, and 'to fix' puts A in to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket that protects against rain.

clue.text: Transport in winter late leaving centre: sound fed up about it

indicators.note: about means the outer word wraps round the cut-down word

parts.note: to sigh is to make a sound of weariness or boredom

indicators.note: leaving centre takes out the middle two letters of the word late

parts.note: taken as written before its middle is removed

explanation.surface: Late in winter, someone stuck in town sighs with boredom about travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving centre' strips AT from the middle, leaving LE; 'about' wraps the sighing word round it. 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer over snow.

clue.text: Old boy withdraws, having got a bit behind in the event

indicators.note: withdraws means the abbreviation for old boy goes backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a trace is a tiny bit

explanation.surface: An old boy pulls out of a race after falling a bit behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdraws' turns the old boy round, giving BO. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames, known as the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the famous annual rowing event between Oxford and Cambridge, called simply the race by Britons.

clue.text: Hateful duo is nothing special

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: special suggests a specially reworked version of the letters

explanation.surface: A hateful pair are nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges the clue's own words into DIOUS; 'nothing' looks like part of the surface but is the zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, something that provokes strong dislike.

clue.text: Seasoning gives taste principally to fish Scotsman rejected

annotationWithheld.why: Seasoning gives taste principally to fish Scotsman rejected (4,4): ROCK (fish) + T (taste principally) fit, but no Scotsman reversed gives SAL; searches found no parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Seasoning gives taste principally to fish Scotsman rejected

clue.text: Several refuse to admit Conservative faction

parts.note: ten is taken loosely as several

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the letter for Conservative goes inside

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

explanation.surface: Several people won't let a Conservative group in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a faction within a political party, as Militant Tendency was within Labour.

clue.text: Power of politician in EU country

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, an EU member
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician holds power in a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a great power, a state ruling over many territories.
